name: K-State TRIGA hottest element: scram and loss of the pool water at 10 s (illustrative)
label: synthetic
citation: Starts from the K-State 1.25 MW hot-element case with the SAR film coefficient (see ksu-triga-1p25mw-film: radii Table 4.6, conductivities Tables 13.3 and 4.6, gap conductance Appendix A, q' from eq. 9, h from eq. 7). Everything after 10 s is ASSUMED, not from the SAR. The heat capacities (a transient needs them) are the ones of the ut-triga-pulse-4p40 case: U-ZrH from the UT-Austin SAR Table 4.1 and stainless steel from the K-State SAR Table 13.3; the same material family, a different reactor's table for the fuel.
description: ILLUSTRATIVE, not a safety analysis. The pin runs at the SAR's 1.25 MW hottest-element state (steady start), then at 10 s the reactor scrams and the pool water is lost: the film coefficient falls from 57.7 kW/m2/K to 100 W/m2/K (air by natural convection, an ASSUMED round number; no radiation is modelled) between 10 and 11 s, and the heat rate falls to an ASSUMED 6.5 % (4.03 kW/m) at 10.5 s and then follows an assumed decay curve (2.5 kW/m at 100 s, 1.6 kW/m at 600 s). The pool-water temperature stays 20 C (the air). The case shows what the lost film does after a scram: the stored heat and the decay heat can no longer reach the pool, so the pin settles near 600 K and is still about 500 K ten minutes later, where with the pool kept it would be within about 55 K of the pool after one minute and a few kelvin after ten. Solid-cylinder model with the zirconium rod ignored; thermal only; the boundary history and the power history are inputs, FEED computes neither a decay curve nor a heat transfer coefficient. One axial slice at the maximum heat flux. No temperature limits are applied here (a limits set can be added in the editor).

thermal.conductivity.source: K-State SAR 2004 Table 13.3 (18 W/m/K, all temperatures); UT-Austin SAR 2023 Table 4.1 (0.18 W/cm/K)

thermal.volumetricHeatCapacity.source: UT-Austin SAR Table 4.1: 2.04 + 0.00417 T[C] J/cm3/K, rewritten in kelvin (a = 2.04e6 - 4170 x 273.15). The SAR states no validity range; 0 to 1000 C is assumed to cover the pulse

thermal.conductivity.source: K-State SAR 2004 Table 13.3 and Table 4.6 (16.6 W/m/K at 400 K)

thermal.volumetricHeatCapacity.source: K-State SAR Table 13.3: 7900 kg/m3 x 477 J/kg/K at 300 K (515 J/kg/K at 400 K: the value rises 8% over 100 K, which matters little for a pulse this short)

gap.source: K-State SAR 2004 section 4.5.3 and Appendix A: effective gap resistance 500 Btu/h/ft2/F = 2840 W/m2/K
